title: Loss of Thrust in Both Engines After Encountering a Flock of Birds and Subsequent Ditching on the Hudson River, US Airways Flight 1549 (NTSB/AAR-10/03)
claim_or_use: Timeline of the January 15 2009 bird strike, engine loss, three-option evaluation (LaGuardia, Teterboro, Hudson), ditching, 155 survivors, 5 seriously injured, probable-cause finding that the ditching decision was appropriate
notes: Primary NTSB final report; used as the book's opening scene.

title: Airbus SAS A320-214, N106US, Lessons Learned
claim_or_use: Corroborating summary of the Flight 1549 bird strike and dual engine loss
notes: Cross-check against the NTSB report for aircraft registration and event summary.

title: Humans and Automation: Use, Misuse, Disuse, Abuse
claim_or_use: Defines misuse (over-reliance/automation bias) and disuse (neglect/under-reliance) as the two failure modes framing the book's central grid
notes: Human Factors 39(2): 230-253. Foundational taxonomy for chapter 2.

title: Ironies of Automation
claim_or_use: The two ironies: automating routine work removes the practice operators need to stay skilled, while leaving them responsible for the rare, hardest interventions
notes: Automatica 19(6); one of the most cited papers in human factors engineering.

title: Ironies of Automation
claim_or_use: Full argument for chapter 3: skill degradation from disuse, vigilance burden, and the paradox of needing more operator training as automation increases
notes: Same source as ch02-002; central text for this chapter.

author_or_institution: Bureau d'Enquêtes et d'Analyses pour la sécurité de l'aviation civile (BEA)
title: Final Report — Accident on 1st June 2009 to the Airbus A330-203 registered F-GZCP operated by Air France, flight AF 447 Rio de Janeiro - Paris
claim_or_use: Pitot-tube icing, autopilot disengagement, pilot confusion and 'startle,' 25 safety recommendations including manual-flying training at altitude
notes: Secondary summary of the BEA final report via IEEE Spectrum; figures cross-checked against NPR and ABC News coverage of the same report.

title: Children of the Magenta Line (training presentation)
claim_or_use: Origin of the 'children of the magenta' term; American Airlines analysis attributing 68% of a set of accidents/incidents/violations to automation mismanagement; the guidance to 'step down' automation levels rather than abandon or over-rely on them
notes: Cross-checked against AOPA's 'Always Learning' retrospective and Air Facts Journal commentary; used descriptively, no invented dialogue from the video.

author_or_institution: Norman H. Mackworth (historical); multiple secondary sources
title: Mackworth Clock / WWII radar vigilance research
claim_or_use: RAF radar operators lost 10-15% detection efficiency within the first 30 minutes of a watch; the Mackworth Clock test and the 'vigilance decrement' finding that detection accuracy declines further over a 2-hour watch
notes: Secondary synthesis (Wikipedia, millisecond.com test documentation) of Mackworth's original 1940s RAF-commissioned studies; original wartime reports are not freely available online, so this chapter treats the figures as a well-established secondary account rather than a primary citation.

author_or_institution: John D. Lee; Katrina A. See
title: Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance
claim_or_use: Conceptual model of trust calibration: the gap between a person's trust in a system and the system's actual trustworthiness, and the design implications of over- and under-calibration
notes: Human Factors 46(1): 50-80; central framework for chapter 6.

author_or_institution: Berkeley J. Dietvorst; Joseph P. Simmons; Cade Massey
title: Algorithm Aversion: People Erroneously Avoid Algorithms After Seeing Them Err
claim_or_use: Five studies showing people lose confidence in an algorithmic forecaster faster than in a human one after watching each err by the same amount, even when the algorithm outperforms overall
notes: Journal of Experimental Psychology: General 144(1): 114-126.

author_or_institution: Berkeley J. Dietvorst; Joseph P. Simmons; Cade Massey
title: Overcoming Algorithm Aversion: People Will Use Imperfect Algorithms If They Can (Even Slightly) Modify Them
claim_or_use: Follow-up finding used as counterevidence/resolution: giving people even minimal ability to adjust an algorithm's output substantially restores willingness to use it
notes: Management Science 64(3): 1155-1170.

author_or_institution: Jennifer M. Logg; Julia A. Minson; Don A. Moore
title: Algorithm Appreciation: People Prefer Algorithmic to Human Judgment
claim_or_use: Six experiments showing lay people adhered more to advice framed as algorithmic than as human; effect present for numeric estimation and forecasting tasks; effect shrank when choosing between an algorithm and one's own judgment, and shrank further for domain experts, who relied less on algorithmic advice than laypeople did and were hurt by it
notes: Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes 151: 90-103.

title: International evaluation of an AI system for breast cancer screening
claim_or_use: AI system trained on UK data (about 76,000 women) generalized to US data (more than 15,000 women); reduced false positives by 5.7% (US) and 1.2% (UK) and false negatives by 9.4% (US) and 2.7% (UK) relative to the original radiologist reads
notes: Nature 577: 89-94. An addendum was later published (Nature 2020, s41586-020-2679-9); note its existence rather than treat the original as unrevised.

author_or_institution: Julia Angwin; Jeff Larson; Surya Mattu; Lauren Kirchner (ProPublica)
title: Machine Bias
claim_or_use: Broward County, Florida COMPAS dataset analysis: among defendants who were not re-arrested, 45% of Black defendants were misclassified as higher risk versus 24% of white defendants; the inverse asymmetry in false 'low risk' labels for white defendants who did reoffend
notes: Secondary summary of the original ProPublica investigation and dataset; Northpointe/Equivant's methodological rebuttal (accuracy-equity and calibration counter-analysis) is used as required counterevidence.

title: State v. Loomis, 881 N.W.2d 749 (Wis. 2016)
claim_or_use: Wisconsin Supreme Court upheld the use of COMPAS at sentencing against a due-process challenge, but held it could not be the determinative factor and required cautionary disclosures about the tool's proprietary, undisclosed scoring method
notes: Case 2015AP157-CR; Eric Loomis pleaded guilty to fleeing an officer and operating a vehicle without owner's consent in connection with a 2013 drive-by shooting investigation.

title: Amazon's algorithmic management of warehouse workers slated
claim_or_use: Description of scanner-based real-time productivity tracking, quota enforcement, and algorithmically generated discipline/termination decisions
notes: Used for mechanism description of algorithmic rate management.

author_or_institution: The Nation / multiple outlets citing Amazon and industry injury data
title: Amazon injury-rate reporting versus warehousing-industry average
claim_or_use: Amazon warehouses recorded over 30% more injuries than the warehousing-industry average in 2023; robotic Amazon facilities showed a 54% higher serious-injury rate than non-robotic facilities in cited research
notes: Cross-checked against New Republic and In These Times coverage of the same underlying injury-rate research and Senate inquiry material.

author_or_institution: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission; U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission
title: Findings Regarding the Market Events of May 6, 2010
claim_or_use: A single large automated sell algorithm (targeting roughly $4.1 billion in E-mini S&P 500 futures at a fixed 9%-of-volume execution rate without regard to price or time) combined with liquidity withdrawal and manipulative spoofing activity to produce the Dow's intraday plunge of about 9% between 2:30 and 3:00pm
notes: Joint SEC-CFTC staff report to the Joint Advisory Committee on Emerging Regulatory Issues, issued September 30, 2010.

title: Knight Capital Group order and $12 million penalty (market access rule violations)
claim_or_use: August 1, 2012 deployment error activated dormant 'Power Peg' legacy code, sending erroneous orders into NYSE-listed securities for roughly 45 minutes and producing an approximately $440 million realized pre-tax loss; SEC fined Knight $12 million for market-access and supervisory violations
notes: Cross-checked against Knight Capital's own 8-K and 10-Q filings for the loss figure and timeline.

author_or_institution: Eleanor A. Maguire; David G. Gadian; Ingrid S. Johnsrude; Catriona D. Good; John Ashburner; Richard S. J. Frackowiak; Christopher D. Frith
title: Navigation-related structural change in the hippocampi of taxi drivers
claim_or_use: London taxi drivers had more posterior-hippocampal gray matter than matched controls, correlated with years of experience; London bus drivers (fixed routes) did not show the same pattern, isolating navigation demand rather than driving itself as the causal factor
notes: PNAS 97(8): 4398-4403. Used as the strongest neuroscientific anchor for the deskilling chapter; the chapter is explicit that broader deskilling claims (calculators, autocorrect, GPS) rest on thinner and more contested evidence than this study.

author_or_institution: Malin Eiband; Daniel Buschek; Alexander Kremer; Heinrich Hussmann
title: The Impact of Placebic Explanations on Trust in Intelligent Systems
claim_or_use: A fabricated ('placebic') explanation produced compliance rates (93%) nearly identical to a genuine explanation (94%) and far above no explanation (60%) when the required user effort was low, showing explanation format alone can move trust independent of explanation content
notes: CHI 2019 Extended Abstracts. Central study for chapter 14's argument that explanation can satisfy without informing.

title: Moral Crumple Zones: Cautionary Tales in Human-Robot Interaction
claim_or_use: Coins 'moral crumple zone': in a joint human-automation system, moral and legal accountability for a failure concentrates on the human operator with the least control, analogous to how a car's crumple zone absorbs impact to protect what's inside
notes: Engaging Science, Technology, and Society 5: 40-60.

title: Highway Accident Report: Collision Between Vehicle Controlled by Developmental Automated Driving System and Pedestrian, Tempe, Arizona, March 18, 2018
claim_or_use: Uber's self-driving test SUV struck and killed 49-year-old pedestrian Elaine Herzberg, who was walking a bicycle outside a crosswalk; the system could not classify a pedestrian outside a crosswalk, correctly recognized an imminent collision only 1.2 seconds before impact, automatic emergency braking was disabled while under computer control, and the safety driver was found to have been watching a video streaming app rather than monitoring the road
notes: Secondary summary of the NTSB final report and public docket; cross-checked against CBC, NBC News, PBS NewsHour, and the Eno Center for Transportation's summary of the earlier preliminary report.

title: Inc.
source_type: Tesla Vehicle Safety Report (quarterly Autopilot safety data)
claim_or_use: First-party safety report
url: Tesla-reported crash rate of roughly one crash per 7.63 million miles driven with Autopilot engaged versus about one crash per 955,000 miles for Tesla vehicles without Autopilot active, with later quarters (including Q3 2025, about one per 6.36 million miles) showing the Autopilot figure worsening for three consecutive quarters
notes: https://www.nextbigfuture.com/2024/07/tesla-autopilot-fsd-and-robotaxi-safety-versus-human.html
column11: First-party Tesla data reported without independent verification of methodology (e.g., what road types and driver populations are included when Autopilot is engaged versus not); the chapter flags this as a limitation rather than treating the comparison as apples-to-apples.

title: Waymo Safety Impact
claim_or_use: Waymo's published driverless-operation data reporting roughly one crash per 50,000 miles in fully driverless operation and a low rate of critical disengagements (about 0.07 per 1,000 miles), with Waymo characterizing most collisions as low-speed and caused by another road user's error or illegal behavior
notes: First-party Waymo data; same caveat as ch16-001 about self-reported methodology and definitional differences between 'disengagement,' 'crash,' and 'critical incident' across companies.

title: Loss of Thrust in Both Engines After Encountering a Flock of Birds and Subsequent Ditching on the Hudson River, US Airways Flight 1549 (NTSB/AAR-10/03)
claim_or_use: Revisited in depth for chapter 17: NTSB's finding that Sullenberger's decision to ditch rather than attempt a return to LaGuardia or diversion to Teterboro was the appropriate call given the altitude and distance available
notes: Same primary source as ch01-001, examined here for the decision-quality finding rather than the narrative opening.

author_or_institution: Qantas; Australian Transport Safety Bureau (secondary reporting)
title: Qantas Flight 32 uncontained engine failure, November 4 2010
source_type: Accident case study (secondary reporting of investigation)
claim_or_use: An uncontained failure in a Rolls-Royce Trent 900 engine over the Riau Islands generated roughly 100 ECAM (Electronic Centralised Aircraft Monitor) checklist messages; a five-pilot crew (present because of a scheduled route check) divided the workload, with Captain Richard de Crespigny making judgment calls the ECAM system could not resolve; the aircraft landed safely at Singapore Changi with no injuries
notes: Secondary synthesis drawing on public accident accounts and de Crespigny's own public statements; used descriptively without invented cockpit dialogue beyond what is publicly documented.

title: Apollo 11 lunar descent 1202/1201 program alarms
source_type: Historical case study (secondary reporting of NASA records)
claim_or_use: During Apollo 11's final descent, the Apollo Guidance Computer twice raised 1202 'executive overflow' alarms; 24-year-old guidance officer support engineer Jack Garman, using a handwritten alarm-code reference sheet, confirmed to guidance officer Steve Bales that the alarm did not require an abort, allowing the landing to proceed
notes: Secondary account synthesizing NASA oral histories and contemporaneous mission records; no invented dialogue beyond documented radio-transcript content.

title: Lion Air Flight 610 final accident investigation report
claim_or_use: October 29, 2018 crash killing 189; MCAS repeatedly activated on erroneous data from a single angle-of-attack sensor and progressively overpowered the flight crew's manual control inputs
notes: Secondary summary of the NTSC final report via CNN; cross-checked against code7700.com's technical case-study summary.

title: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 accident investigation
claim_or_use: March 10, 2019 crash near Ejere, Ethiopia, killing all 157 aboard shortly after takeoff from Addis Ababa; left angle-of-attack sensor diverged sharply from the right (reaching about 74.5 degrees versus 15.3 degrees), again triggering repeated MCAS activation consistent with the Lion Air 610 failure pattern
notes: Cross-checked against Al Jazeera's contemporaneous reporting and the NTSB's later public comments (2023) on Ethiopia's final report.

title: NTSB Publishes Additional Comments on Ethiopia's Final Report on 737 MAX 8 Accident
claim_or_use: Both 737 MAX accidents led to the type's worldwide grounding and a mandated redesign of MCAS, including reliance on both angle-of-attack sensors and revised crew procedures and training
notes: Used to establish the regulatory aftermath and correction, required as counterevidence that institutions did respond.

author_or_institution: Raja Parasuraman; Thomas B. Sheridan; Christopher D. Wickens
title: A Model for Types and Levels of Human Interaction with Automation
claim_or_use: Four automation-function classes (information acquisition, information analysis, decision/action selection, action implementation) crossed with ten graduated levels each, replacing an all-or-nothing view of automation with a design framework for choosing how much and what kind of automation a task needs
notes: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics — Part A 30(3): 286-297. Central framework for chapter 19's design argument.

author_or_institution: John D. Lee; Katrina A. See
title: Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance
claim_or_use: Design-facing conclusions revisited for chapter 19: closing the calibration gap between trust and trustworthiness through system design, training, and feedback rather than through blanket trust or blanket suspicion
notes: Same source as ch06-001, drawn on again here for its design recommendations rather than its diagnostic framework.
